title: Original JANUS 2026 SQLite historical backups, corrupt exclusion and low-I/O custody

preservation_policy.reason: Three 1.45GB backups would require over 4GB of NAS reads; user prefers the NAS to avoid sustained I/O, and exact equality cannot be inferred from file sizes.
preservation_policy.approved_future_test: One separately selected snapshot using an owner-scheduled off-peak, read-only SQLite integrity and WAL-aware validation, without accessing credentials or publishing rows.

recovery_recommendations: Keep all three 1.45GB source snapshots intact; identical sizes are not proof of identical contents.
Do not blindly copy a live SQLite DB without consistent backup/WAL semantics.
Extract exact schemas and redacted aggregate structure before attempting any private-only migration.
Use SHA-256 streaming in an explicit off-peak slot if needed; do not run full-disk background scrapes.
Do not import raw vault/chat/memory data into publicly indexed HRAiN or Meta Registry.
Do not reinterpret old performance logs as scientific model validation.
useful_current_repositories: janus-meta-registry: schema, provenance, private archive pointers
HRAiN and iNaiHR: potential read-only semantic history adapter after privacy filtering
Janus-Demiurge: isolated historical DB writer and original MicroGPT source, not weights
